A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffSampling and retain identifiable methods, experiments and datasets. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial revision and relocation of material.

before.justification: V1 reports original math-solving, XSum summarization and divergent association task results, including parameter ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original results on the retained tasks, with additional temperature experiments, ablations and qualitative analyses in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: V2 removes DiffSampling-reparam and its gamma-based probability adjustment, replacing it with DiffSampling-minp, which constrains truncation using a threshold relative to the highest token probability. It also introduces temperature scaling after truncation into the proposed procedure. DiffSampling-cut and the lower-bound mechanism remain.

E1.justification: MetaMathQA, GSM8K, MATH, XSum and DAT coverage is retained; MetaMathQA evaluation moves to Appendix C.1. The limited addition is the standalone next-token completion case using an NLG-definition prompt in v2 Section 4/Table 1, rather than a new benchmark suite.

E2.justification: V2 adds min-p sampling as an evaluated baseline across the existing tasks. Greedy, contrastive search, eta-sampling, locally typical sampling and nucleus sampling remain; nucleus is renamed top-p, and its higher-temperature comparisons remain in Appendix C. Contrastive decoding is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 expands temperature evaluation to 0.6, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 10.0 across multiple methods and adds controlled comparisons of scaling before versus after truncation. It adds SimCSE-based coherence evaluation for XSum and revises both DAT prompts by adding an answer prefix. These are documented protocol changes, not merely additional settings disclosed for unchanged experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds temperature-order controls, broader temperature sensitivity tests, min-p parameter ablations, qualitative output comparisons and DAT noun-overlap heatmaps. V1's gamma/reparameterization studies and MetaMathQA lower-bound sweep are removed. The other lower-bound studies are retained and revised in Appendix D.2.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed math and summarization results, using standard errors and 95% confidence intervals for the same respective metric categories. Both use 100 DAT trials for non-greedy strategies and boxplots. Additional rows and changed uncertainty values do not establish a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: At the stated unit temperature, DiffSampling-cut accuracy changes from 67.10% to 66.36% on GSM8K and from 21.06% to 21.38% on MATH (v1 Tables 2–3; v2 Table 2). Semantic scores are widely revised: greedy instructed-XSum similarity changes from 0.14 to 0.49 despite the same stated embedding model. V2 adds min-p, coherence, temperature and qualitative results while removing reparameterization results. Revised DAT prompts preclude interpreting its changed outcomes as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The discrete-derivative definition in Equation 1 remains. V1's reparameterization equation and gamma-limit discussion are removed; v2 introduces the min-p threshold definition and an unproved cutoff/support assertion, argmin(Delta p) <= D. Neither version provides a formal theorem or proof establishing truncation correctness.

C1.justification: The contribution changes from truncation plus probability reparameterization to truncation with two relaxation mechanisms. The abstract and conclusion drop the contribution of directly boosting low-probability tokens through reparameterization and emphasize excluding incorrect tokens. V2 also advances correctness-preservation claims for temperature scaling after truncation, while retaining the overall quality-and-diversity objective.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the interpretation of gamma-driven exploration with an argument that truncation permits temperature increases while preserving correctness, and adds min-p-specific operating guidance. Its limitations newly address short generated outputs, uncertain applicability to longer generation, automatic metrics' disagreement with human judgments and the absence of human evaluation. Existing model-bias and memorization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promise of a future code release with a specified anonymous repository link and adds an H100 GPU to the two L40 GPUs documented in Appendix A. Conversely, it omits v1's exact GSM8K/MATH evaluation counts and separate training-data prompt. These documentation changes do not establish that the underlying sample sizes changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against min-p and contrastive decoding, together with citations supporting quality-diversity trade-offs, SimCSE, the illustrative model and automatic-metric limitations. DiffSampling is now positioned as refining both top-p and min-p truncation. Most of the earlier background and cited work remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, method presentation and results discussion are extensively rewritten. Separate illustrative-example and discussion sections reorganize the main narrative, MetaMathQA results move to the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized around temperature experiments, ablations and qualitative analysis. Terminology also changes from nucleus to top-p and Sent-BERT to SBERT.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1 for the revised method family, merges separate GSM8K/MATH and instructed/pre-trained XSum tables into side-by-side displays, and revises DAT plots and legends. It adds temperature plots, before/after comparison tables, noun-overlap heatmaps and extensive qualitative tables, while removing the gamma-study displays.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through min-p comparisons, temperature-order controls, coherence evaluation and qualitative examples, and states clearer limitations. However, substantial semantic-score revisions remain unexplained despite unchanged stated metric definitions. Its Algorithm 1 computes temperature-scaled logits but applies softmax to probs, conflicting with the described procedure, while stronger correctness guarantees remain heuristic. These benefits and unresolved inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment of the net change in overall quality.
